html:
The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556 between the army of the boy emperor Akbar and that of Hemu, a Hindu general who had made himself king in Delhi. The Mughal win secured the Mughal Empire for the next two centuries.

The Mughals had only just come back. Humayun, driven out of India by Sher Shah Suri in 1540, retook Delhi in 1555 and died the next January after a fall on his library stairs. Akbar was thirteen, and his guardian Bairam Khan ruled for him.

Hemu had risen from a seller of saltpetre to chief minister of the last Sur king and had won twenty-two battles. In October 1556 he drove the Mughal garrison out of Delhi and took the royal title Vikramaditya.

The armies met on the same plain where Babur had won thirty years before (see the First Battle of Panipat). Hemu had 1,500 war elephants and the larger force, but Mughal riders had captured his guns days earlier. His elephants were breaking the Mughal wings when an arrow hit him in the eye. Seeing him fall, his army fled.

He was brought to Akbar's tent unconscious and beheaded. Delhi and Agra fell at once.
